title_en: Zeng Yongfu v. Dongguan Yixin Magnetic Disk Co., Ltd., Wang Zhi, et al. — dispute over rewards and remuneration for service invention creators and designers
ruling_gist_en: In a dispute over remuneration for inventors of service invention-creations, when determining whether the unit that has been granted the patent right has implemented the service invention-creation, a statement made by the unit in an infringement lawsuit that the patent product involved has economic benefits shall be considered a statement of objective fact by the unit. In accordance with the principle of good faith, it is presumed that the unit has in fact implemented the patented technical solution. The damages obtained by the unit through rights enforcement actions based on the patent in question constitute income received by the patentee from prohibiting others from practicing the patent without permission. After deducting necessary enforcement costs and expenses, such economic benefits shall be regarded as operating profit as referred to in Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, and on this basis, reasonable remuneration shall be given to the service inventor.

full_text_en:
Zeng Yongfu v. Dongguan Yixin Magnetic Disc Co., Ltd., Wang Zhi, et al. — dispute over rewards and remuneration for inventors or designers of service invention creations

【Ruling Summary】

In a dispute over remuneration for inventors of service invention creations, when determining whether the entity to which the patent is granted has actually implemented the service invention creation, the entity's statement in an infringement lawsuit that the patent-involved product has economic benefits shall be considered a statement of objective facts by the entity. According to the principle of good faith, it is presumed that the entity has implemented the technical solution of the patent-involved invention. The damages received by the entity from rights enforcement activities based on the patent-involved invention constitute income obtained by the patentee from prohibiting others from exploiting the patent without permission. After deducting necessary rights enforcement costs and expenses, such economic benefits shall be deemed as the operating profit referred to in Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, and reasonable remuneration shall be given to the service inventor on this basis.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme Court IP Civil Final No. 230

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Dongguan Yixin Magnetic Disc Co., Ltd. Address: Fuda Industrial Zone, Zhangyang Village, Zhangmutou Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Yiming, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Wen, lawyer from Shanghai Xinsong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Liu, lawyer from Shanghai Xinsong Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zeng Yongfu, male, born on November 24, 1972, Han Chinese, residing in Xihu District, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Daolong, lawyer from Guangdong Taixu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Fa, lawyer from Guangdong Taixu Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Wang Zhi, male, born on December 10, 1959, Han Chinese, residing in Lianhu District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yuanwei, lawyer from Guangdong Shangkuan (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Xu Yiming, male, born on March 14, 1964, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yuanwei, lawyer from Guangdong Shangkuan (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

The appellant, Dongguan Yixin Magnetic Disc Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yixin Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2017) Yue 73 Min Chu No. 3581 rendered by the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court on May 21, 2019, in the case of dispute over rewards and remuneration for inventors or designers of service invention creations between the respondent Zeng Yongfu and the third parties at first instance Xu Yiming and Wang Zhi. After the case was docketed on July 22, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on December 18, 2019. The agent ad litem of the appellant Yixin Company, Jiang Wen, the agent ad litem of the respondent Zeng Yongfu, Xu Fa, and the agent ad litem of the third parties at first instance Xu Yiming and Wang Zhi, Wang Yuanwei, appeared in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Yixin Company's appeal requests: to set aside the original judgment and amend the judgment to reject all of Zeng Yongfu's claims. Facts and reasons:

(I) The basic facts found by the original trial court are erroneous. 1. Yixin Company did not implement the utility model patent with patent number ZL200720051806.9 and titled "Portable Refillable Spray Bottle" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-involved invention). The original trial court's finding that the patent-involved invention had been implemented is erroneous. After sample production of products based on the technology of the patent-involved invention, liquid leakage was discovered. From a commercial perspective, Yixin Company could not have implemented a technically backward technical solution that would generate no economic benefits but rather cause losses. Within three years after the patent application for the patent-involved invention, Yixin Company continuously improved the technology and only basically developed a product capable of implementation in 2010. Yixin Company's rights enforcement cases were also concentrated around this time. Yixin Company's statement in lawsuits against others for infringement of the patent-involved invention that it had implemented the patent-involved invention was made for litigation strategy considerations. The evidence submitted by Yixin Company in the original trial court, including the utility model patent documents for patent number ZL200820206225.2 titled "Improved Portable Refillable Spray Bottle" (hereinafter referred to as the 2008 patent) and patent number ZL201120522423.1 titled "A Refillable Spray Bottle" (hereinafter referred to as the 2011 patent), as well as comparison charts of patent technology improvements, was to rebut statements unfavorable to itself, and there was no act of violating good faith or abusing litigation rights. In contrast, Zeng Yongfu fabricated the fact that Yixin Company had already paid the third party at first instance Wang Zhi RMB 1,000,000, which violates good faith. 2. When Zeng Yongfu filed the lawsuit, he admitted that his employment start date was November 2006, but the original trial court found it to be June 2006, which is erroneous. During the period from June 2006 to November 2006, Zeng Yongfu worked for a related company of Yixin Company. Both companies are independent legal persons, and there was no internal transfer within a group company. 3. According to Yixin Company's own statistics, the damages obtained from lawsuits against others for infringement of the patent-involved invention were only RMB 885,000, not the RMB 1,125,000 found by the original trial court. The original trial court did not consider that after a victorious judgment, the actual amount received by Yixin Company through compulsory enforcement procedures was only RMB 376,784, and it ignored the inevitable rights enforcement costs incurred by Yixin Company in infringement lawsuits, including attorney fees of RMB 499,719, and notarization fees, litigation fees, travel expenses, etc., totaling RMB 176,274. As a result, Yixin Company ultimately did not profit from rights enforcement but instead made a net investment of RMB 299,209.

(II) The original trial court considered erroneous and omitted facts when determining the remuneration for inventors of service invention creations (hereinafter referred to as service invention remuneration). 1. The original trial court erroneously found that the remuneration for the patent-involved service invention should be divided into three equal shares. The patent-involved invention was developed based on the patented technical solution provided by an Israeli in 2004, which played the most significant role in the patent-involved invention. Zeng Yongfu only transferred to the R&D department as deputy manager on September 1, 2008, while the patent-involved invention was applied for on May 23, 2007. Therefore, Zeng Yongfu lacked the technical capability to contribute to the patent-involved invention. 2. The original trial court should not have used the damages obtained by Yixin Company from infringement lawsuits based on the patent-involved invention as the basis for measuring remuneration. Yixin Company incurred huge rights enforcement costs, and the compensation amounts awarded were merely receivables. The actual amounts received by Yixin Company, after deducting rights enforcement costs, were negative. Yixin Company enforced its rights based on the patent-involved invention to combat counterfeiting and stop infringements, not to obtain income through rights enforcement.

(III) The original trial court erred in applying the law. 1. Regarding the statute of limitations. The starting point for Zeng Yongful's claim for service invention remuneration should be December 31 of each calendar year. According to the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law), Zeng Yongfu should have known that his rights were infringed by December 31 of each year at the latest. Therefore, the statute of limitations for his claim for service invention remuneration should also be calculated with December 31 of each calendar year as the boundary. This case should apply the statute of limitations before the implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), that is, the two-year limitation period, not three years. In summary, even if this case supports Zeng Yongfu's right to receive remuneration, the period for which he can receive remuneration should be from January 1, 2015, to May 23, 2017. 2. The original trial court misinterpreted the term "implementation" in Articles 76 and 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law. "Implementation" here should mean actual placement in the market. The original trial court's determination that Yixin Company had engaged in implementation solely because Yixin Company had filed infringement lawsuits based on the patent-involved invention is clearly inconsistent with the facts and does not conform to the legislative intent of the Patent Law. Since Yixin Company did not engage in "implementation," it did not obtain profits or economic benefits, and therefore should not pay service invention remuneration.

Zeng Yongfu argued: The original trial court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Yixin Company's appeal requests have no factual or legal basis. 1. The original trial court correctly found that the total amount of infringement damages awarded in support of the patent-involved invention through judgments was RMB 1,125,000. According to the judgments submitted by Yixin Company in the second instance regarding rights enforcement of the patent-involved invention, the total compensation amount reached RMB 1,585,000. Yixin Company has no evidence to prove its claims of high rights enforcement costs in infringement lawsuits and inadequate enforcement proceeds. Moreover, the original trial court's discretionary award of RMB 200,000 for service invention remuneration was already far lower than the economic benefits brought to Yixin Company by implementing the patent-involved invention. 2. The patent-involved invention has been implemented. Yixin Company claimed in its patent enforcement lawsuits that the patent-involved invention was implemented, and infringing products existed in those infringement lawsuits, indicating that the patent-involved invention could be implemented and had been placed on the market. 3. The patent document of the patent-involved invention already records Zeng Yongfu as an inventor. Yixin Company's claim that Zeng Yongfu lacked technical capability is not supported by sufficient evidence. The manner in which the original trial court exercised its discretion to determine the amount of service invention remuneration reflects the principle of fairness and complies with the law. 4. The term of the patent-involved invention expired on May 23, 2017. According to Articles 76 and 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, the statute of limitations for Zeng Yongfu's claim for a one-time payment of service invention remuneration from Yixin Company should start from May 23, 2017. Zeng Yongfu filed the lawsuit with the original trial court on October 11, 2017, which did not exceed the statute of limitations.

The third parties at first instance, Wang Zhi and Xu Yiming, stated: The original trial court's discretionary determination that Yixin Company should pay service invention remuneration lacks factual basis, and they request the judgment to be amended to reject Zeng Yongfu's claims. (I) The patent-involved invention is not implementable and it is impossible to determine whether it generated operating profits. The original trial court found that the patent-involved invention had been implemented based on the infringement lawsuits filed by Yixin Company. However, the patent-involved invention had a technical defect of liquid leakage and was not implementable. Through the efforts of the two third parties at first instance, a series of subsequent inventions were made, and it was not until 2011 that the product of the 2011 patent could be mass-produced. Since the patent-involved invention was not implemented and could not have profited, Yixin Company should not pay service invention remuneration to Zeng Yongfu. (II) Although Zeng Yongfu's name appears as an inventor on the patent-involved invention, he did not play an actual role. The main technical concept of the patent-involved invention was proposed by the two third parties at first instance. Zeng Yongfu was only responsible for project follow-up and did not make technical contributions. (III) The original trial court determined Yixin Company's profit based on the compensation amounts awarded in judgments from Yixin Company's rights enforcement based on the patent-involved invention. However, compensation for rights enforcement does not equal profits from patent implementation, and the original trial court did not consider Yixin Company's rights enforcement costs. (IV) The original trial court considered that there were three inventors of the patent-involved invention but did not consider that the three did not play equal roles. When Zeng Yongfu joined the company, the two third parties at first instance had already conducted technical experiments. After the patent-involved invention was granted, Zeng Yongfu left the company. Zeng Yongfu played only the most minor auxiliary role in the patent-involved invention.

Zeng Yongfu filed a lawsuit with the original trial court, which accepted the case on October 11, 2017. Zeng Yongfu's claims at first instance: 1. Order Yixin Company to pay Zeng Yongfu service invention remuneration of RMB 1,000,000; 2. All litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Yixin Company. Facts and reasons: Zeng Yongfu started working at Yixin Company in November 2006, serving as Deputy Manager of the Engineering Department, with job responsibilities including participating in technology R&D projects and technology development. During his tenure, as the person in charge of Yixin Company's technology R&D projects, Zeng Yongfu completed multiple R&D tasks. Among them, the patent-involved invention, led by Zeng Yongfu, was applied for by Yixin Company and granted. Relying on this patent, Yixin Company successfully transformed and made huge profits by selling related patented products through Dongguan Zhenglisi Commercial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongguan Zhenglisi Company) and Zhenglisi International Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenglisi Company), which were actually controlled by its legal representative Xu Yiming. After the patent-involved invention was granted, Yixin Company did not pay any rewards or remuneration to Zeng Yongfu, seriously infringing upon Zeng Yongfu's lawful rights and interests. Therefore, Zeng Yongfu filed this lawsuit.

Yixin Company argued at first instance: 1. Zeng Yongfu only played an auxiliary and minor role in the proposal, development, and completion of the technical solution of the patent-involved invention. Before Zeng Yongfu joined Yixin Company, the third parties at first instance, Xu Yiming and Wang Zhi, were already studying the technical solution of the patent-involved invention. After joining Yixin Company, Zeng Yongfu did not engage in R&D work and did not play a role in the conception and proposal of the patent-involved invention. The actual technical R&D work was carried out by Xu Yiming and Wang Zhi. 2. The patent-involved invention was merely an experiment in Yixin Company's continuous R&D process for portable refillable spray bottles. Due to the unreasonable exhaust structure of the patent-involved invention technology, samples leaked liquid. This significant technical defect meant that the patent-involved invention was never implemented. Yixin Company's statements in lawsuits against others for infringement based on the patent-involved invention that the patent had been implemented were made solely for the convenience of litigation. 3. Dongguan Zhenglisi Company and Zhenglisi Company are completely independent legal persons from Yixin Company. Yixin Company did not obtain profits from selling the patent-involved invention products through these two companies. 4. This case is already time-barred. This case is a dispute over a claim for remuneration. If calculated from the date Zeng Yongfu left his job, the two-year statute of limitations for his claim would have expired on October 25, 2010; if calculated from the date Zeng Yongfu discovered his rights were infringed (October 21, 2013), the statute of limitations would have expired on October 21, 2015. According to the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, service invention remuneration is paid annually and constitutes a segmented claim for remuneration. It should be calculated backwards for two years from the date Zeng Yongfu asserted his rights, i.e., the date of Yixin Company's defense on September 26, 2017. Since the patent-involved invention expired on May 23, 2017, the period during which Zeng Yongfu's claim was not extinguished was from September 26, 2015, to May 23, 2017. 5. Yixin Company's statements in other cases for the convenience of litigation do not constitute an admission in this case. Zeng Yongfu still bears the burden of proof corresponding to his claims.

Wang Zhi argued at first instance: The design and R&D of the patent-involved invention were primarily carried out by Wang Zhi and Xu Yiming. Other participants, including Zeng Yongfu, played auxiliary and coordinating roles. Since the patent-involved invention was granted, it was never actually put into production or implemented. Wang Zhi never received any remuneration or rewards from the implementation of this patent.

Xu Yiming argued at first instance: The technical concept and design of the patent-involved invention were mainly completed by Wang Zhi and Xu Yiming. It was developed and improved based on the 2004 patented technical solution provided by an Israeli. At Yixin Company, Zeng Yongfu served as the head of the Engineering Department, responsible for project follow-up and work coordination. For the convenience of Zeng Yongfu's job promotion, career development, and work motivation, Yixin Company listed Zeng Yongfu as one of the inventors of the patent-involved invention. After the patent-involved invention was granted, technical defects were discovered during actual sample production; the samples leaked liquid, so the patent-involved invention could not be implemented.

The original trial court found the following facts: On May 23, 2007, Yixin Company filed a patent application for the patent-involved invention with the State Intellectual Property Office, and it was granted on May 7, 2008. The patent certificate lists the inventors as Xu Yiming, Zeng Yongfu, and Wang Zhi, and the patentee as Yixin Company. The term of the patent-involved invention expired on May 23, 2017.

The patent claims of the patent-involved invention contain 9 claims: 1. A portable refillable spray bottle, comprising a nozzle assembly, an inner bottle, and a housing; the nozzle assembly is installed on the upper part of the inner bottle, characterized in that a refilling structure is provided at the bottom of the inner bottle, said refilling structure comprising a refilling port at the bottom of the inner bottle, a push rod installed in the refilling port, a push rod return structure, and a sealing structure; said push rod is provided with a refilling channel; the inner bottle is also provided with an exhaust structure. 2. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1, characterized in that the outlet of the refilling channel is located on the side of the push rod and communicates with the refilling port; the top end of the push rod forms a limiting block, and said limiting block is provided with a first sealing ring. 3. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1, characterized in that said exhaust structure is a top exhaust groove provided on the upper part of the inner bottle. 4. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1 or 3, characterized in that said exhaust structure comprises an exhaust hole provided at the bottom of the inner bottle and an air guide tube connected to the exhaust hole and extending to the top of the inner bottle, such that air above is discharged through the exhaust hole at the bottom via the air guide tube. 5. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1, characterized in that said sealing structure comprises a first sealing ring installed on the limiting block of the push rod and a second sealing ring located below the outlet of the refilling channel of the push rod. 6. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 5, characterized in that the upper part of the refilling port at the bottom of the inner bottle is V-shaped, and correspondingly, said first sealing ring is a V-shaped sealing ring. 7. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1 or 5, characterized in that a first step surface is provided inside the refilling port, the second sealing ring and a sealing gasket are located below the first step surface, and said push rod return structure comprises a spring sleeved over the push rod, and the spring is clamped between the sealing gasket and the lower part of the push rod, in a compressed state. 8. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1, characterized in that said nozzle assembly is connected to the inner bottle via a snap-fit structure. 9. The portable refillable spray bottle according to claim 1, characterized in that a window is provided on the housing for observing the remaining liquid level in the inner bottle. According to the utility model patent search report for the patent-involved invention issued by the State Intellectual Property Office on September 9, 2010, the search conclusion was that claims 1-9 have novelty, claims 4-8 have inventiveness, and claims 1-3 and 9 lack inventiveness.

Based on the case summary data submitted by Yixin Company and the results of the original trial court's search for judgments using the patent-involved invention patent number as a keyword on the China Judgments Online website, during the period from 2011 to 2016, Yixin Company filed multiple infringement lawsuits against different defendants based on the alleged infringement of the patent-involved invention. In most cases, Yixin Company claimed to determine the scope of protection of its patent rights based on claims 1, 2, and 4 of the patent-involved invention, and asserted that after the patent-involved invention product was placed on the market, due to its strong practicality and other characteristics, it was favored by consumers and brought economic benefits to Yixin Company. Each defendant, without Yixin Company's permission, implemented the patent-involved invention, infringing upon Yixin Company's lawful rights and interests and causing significant economic losses. The final results of the above cases were that the technical features of the accused infringing products were identical to all technical features of claims 1, 2, and 4 of the patent-involved invention. Each defendant was found to have committed infringement, ordered to cease infringement, and to pay Yixin Company economic losses and reasonable expenses ranging from RMB 8,000 to RMB 500,000. According to Yixin Company's own statistics, the total amount of infringement damages awarded in support through judgments in these lawsuits was RMB 1,125,000.

Zeng Yongfu joined Yixin Company in June 2006 and left in October 2008. During his tenure, he served as Engineering Department Section Chief and Deputy Project Manager, among other positions. According to the Employee Training Agreement, Work Matters Table, and Personnel Change Application Form submitted by Yixin Company, Zeng Yongfu was selected by Yixin Company to participate in a training course on "New Product R&D Process Optimization and R&D Project Management" on August 25-26, 2007; from September 1, 2007, Zeng Yongfu served as Deputy Manager in the Development Department, with daily work matters including assisting engineers in evaluating customer drawings, participating in mold evaluation with engineers, reviewing the distribution of internal drawing documents, urging engineers to follow up on mold development, reviewing mold production specifications and other documents in the Development Department, communicating on development matters with other departments, assisting production/supervisors with difficult issues when necessary, assisting Procurement and PMC in finding outsourced manufacturers and evaluating them, and providing technical support; on June 1, 2008, Zeng Yongfu was transferred to the R&D Department as R&D Manager due to work needs. The main reason for the transfer stated that he had experience in product development and possessed the ability for product structure/design/quoting/drawing review, had an interest in product R&D, and could independently handle external clients and structural issues.

Regarding the division of labor among the three inventors recorded in the bibliographic data of the patent-in-suit, Wang Zhi stated at the first-instance trial that he was responsible for providing the concept principle, Xu Yiming assisted in providing the concept, and Zeng Yongfu was responsible for specific implementation; Xu Yiming stated that he provided funding and development conditions, and the concept of the patent-in-suit was jointly completed by him and Wang Zhi, while Zeng Yongfu was only responsible for follow-up and coordination and did not directly participate in technical design, with the specific implementation being handled by engineers under Zeng Yongfu; Zeng Yongfu acknowledged the division of labor described by Wang Zhi and believed that he led the specific implementation work, with the engineers under him only providing assistance.

During the first-instance trial, Wang Zhi and Xu Yiming applied to participate in the litigation as third parties without independent claims on the grounds that, as joint inventors of the patent-in-suit, they had the right to receive remuneration for service inventions and had a direct interest in the case. Wang Zhi submitted his undergraduate degree certificate in Industrial Electrical Automation and his engineer professional title certificate, intending to prove that he had a professional educational background and R&D capabilities and played a major role in the patent-in-suit; Xu Yiming submitted five invention and utility model patent documents listing himself and Wang Zhi as inventors, as well as a decision on a request for invalidation, intending to prove that he and Wang Zhi had professional technical capabilities, that the patent-in-suit was completed under their leadership, and that Zeng Yongfu only played a supporting role.

Zeng Yongfu filed this lawsuit on October 11, 2017, claiming that the amount of remuneration he should receive should be estimated by reference to the remuneration paid by Yixin Company to Wang Zhi and the actual commercial behavior of Yixin Company licensing others to implement the patent-in-suit, and asserting that Yixin Company paid Wang Zhi RMB 1,000,000 in remuneration for the patent-in-suit. Wang Zhi denied this, claiming that Yixin Company only paid normal wages and did not pay any remuneration or reward for the patent-in-suit; Yixin Company claimed that the patent-in-suit had not been implemented, so no remuneration or reward was paid to Wang Zhi.

Zeng Yongfu claimed that Yixin Company successfully transformed by relying on the patent-in-suit and obtained huge profits through the sale of related products by Dongguan Zhenlisi Company and Zhenlisi Company, which were actually controlled by its legal representative, Xu Yiming. To this end, Zeng Yongfu submitted a report from the digital edition of Southern Metropolis Daily, which mainly stated that Yixin Company was originally a traditional OEM factory and later successfully transformed by relying on a new technology for packaging perfume; Zhenlisi Company is the parent company of Yixin Company, founded by Xu Yiming's brothers and an Israeli woman. Zhenlisi Company developed a lightweight perfume bottle named Travalo and applied for patents in European and American countries, with the product market mainly in Europe and America. In response, Yixin Company argued that the above evidence could not prove that Xu Yiming actually controlled Dongguan Zhenlisi Company and Zhenlisi Company. Xu Yiming was a director of Zhenlisi Company, not a shareholder, and had no relationship with Dongguan Zhenlisi Company; moreover, the above news report contained many statements inconsistent with the facts. The patent mentioned in the report was not the patent-in-suit, and the patent-in-suit had never applied for patents in European or American countries and had never been implemented.

To prove the economic benefits obtained by Yixin Company from implementing the patent-in-suit, Zeng Yongfu submitted an Application for Investigation and Evidence Collection to the first-instance court, requesting the court to obtain the corporate financial annual reports of Yixin Company and Dongguan Zhenlisi Company from 2007 to 2016.

To prove that the patented technology had defects and could not be implemented, Yixin Company submitted the patent documents for the aforementioned 2008 patent and 2011 patent, as well as a comparison chart of the technical features of the patent-in-suit and the above patents. Yixin Company claimed that after the patent-in-suit was filed, it had been continuously improving the technical solution and applying for patents, and claimed that since 2013, it had implemented the 2011 patent. The comparison chart showed that the exhaust pipe of the patent-in-suit directly led to the outside of the bottle body, and the exhaust was uncontrolled. When the pressure inside the bottle increased or the bottle was placed horizontally and the exhaust pipe was submerged by liquid, liquid would leak out through the exhaust pipe. The exhaust passage of the 2008 patent led to the outside through a liquid-filling structure controlled by an exhaust switch. A sealing ring was provided on the liquid-filling structure valve, and the liquid-filling valve could drive the sealing ring to move, so the exhaust passage was controlled. In the 2011 patent, the exhaust passage of the liquid-filling and exhaust structure-related parts was formed by a single injection molding of the injection mold, requiring no secondary processing, with low processing costs and convenient assembly. In addition, Yixin Company also submitted several invention and utility model patent documents, claiming that because the technology of the patent-in-suit was immature, it had been continuously engaged in technological R&D related to the patent-in-suit, constantly improving the technology of the patent-in-suit between 2008 and 2017, and correspondingly filed more than ten invention and utility model patents.

Dongguan Zhenlisi Company is a limited liability company established on April 20, 2012, with Xu Bingleng as its legal representative and Zhenlisi Company as its shareholder.

The first-instance court held that this case was a dispute over remuneration for service invention creators. Based on the claims and defenses of both parties and the facts of the case, the issues in dispute were: (1) whether Zeng Yongfu's filing of this lawsuit had exceeded the statute of limitations; (2) whether Zeng Yongfu had the right to request Yixin Company to pay remuneration for a service invention; (3) if Zeng Yongfu had the right to request payment of remuneration for a service invention, how to determine the amount.

(1) Whether Zeng Yongfu's filing of this lawsuit had exceeded the statute of limitations.

Zeng Yongfu claimed remuneration for a service invention creator. The right to claim remuneration for a service invention is a right of claim, which is subject to the statute of limitations. The statute of limitations should begin to run from the time Zeng Yongfu knew or should have known that he had the right to claim the remuneration.

Regarding the starting point of the statute of limitations. Articles 76 and 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provide that the unit that is granted the patent right may agree with the inventor or designer on the method and amount of remuneration, or stipulate them in its legally formulated internal rules and regulations. If there is no agreement between the parties or stipulation in the unit's internal rules and regulations on the method and amount of remuneration, within the term of the patent right, after the invention-creation patent is exploited, the unit that is granted the patent right shall pay remuneration to the inventor or designer annually, or pay a lump-sum remuneration to the inventor or designer. In this case, since neither party submitted evidence to prove that there was an agreement between the parties on the payment of remuneration for the service invention, or that Yixin Company's internal rules and regulations contained relevant content on remuneration for service inventions, according to the above provisions, after the patent-in-suit was exploited, within the term of the patent right, Yixin Company should pay remuneration to the inventor. Now, Zeng Yongfu requested Yixin Company to pay a lump-sum remuneration. The statute of limitations should begin to run from the expiration of the term of the patent-in-suit, i.e., May 23, 2017. Therefore, Zeng Yongfu filed the lawsuit with the first-instance court on October 11, 2017, which did not exceed the three-year statute of limitations provided in Article 188 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law. His litigation rights were legally protected. Yixin Company's defense that the lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations was unfounded in law, and the first-instance court did not accept it.

(2) Whether Zeng Yongfu had the right to request Yixin Company to pay remuneration for a service invention.

Article 16 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) provides: "The unit that is granted the patent right shall reward the inventor or designer of a service invention-creation; after the patent for invention-creation is exploited, the unit shall give the inventor or designer a reasonable remuneration based on the scope of its application and the economic benefits it yields." According to the above provisions, the unit that is granted the patent right shall give remuneration to the inventor or designer of a service invention-creation after the patent is exploited. In this case, the disputed issues between the parties were: first, whether Zeng Yongfu was an inventor of the patent-in-suit; second, whether the patent-in-suit had been exploited.

Regarding whether Zeng Yongfu was an inventor of the patent-in-suit. The patent-in-suit was filed on May 23, 2007, and granted as a utility model patent by the Patent Office of the PRC on May 7, 2008. According to the patent certificate and the authorized text of the patent-in-suit issued by the Patent Office, Zeng Yongfu was one of the inventors of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, Zeng Yongfu had the right to claim remuneration for a service invention from Yixin Company in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement between the parties. Yixin Company argued that Zeng Yongfu did not engage in R&D work after joining Yixin Company and only played an auxiliary and secondary role in the proposal, development, and completion of the patent-in-suit, so he was not the actual inventor of the patent-in-suit. In response, the first-instance court held that: First, the information recorded in the patent bibliographic data has a public notice effect. In the absence of other contrary evidence to overturn it, the inventor recorded in the patent bibliographic data should be recognized as the actual inventor of the patent. The bibliographic data of the patent-in-suit recorded the inventors as Xu Yiming, Zeng Yongfu, and Wang Zhi. Therefore, in the absence of other contrary evidence, it should be recognized that Zeng Yongfu was one of the inventors of the patent-in-suit. Second, Yixin Company argued that Zeng Yongfu was not an inventor of the patent-in-suit and should bear the burden of proof for this claim. The evidence submitted by Yixin Company in the litigation, such as the Employee Training Agreement, Work Matters Table, and Personnel Change Application Form, were all dated after the filing date of the patent-in-suit, i.e., after the completion of the patent-in-suit, and could not prove the actual distribution of work during the completion of the patent-in-suit. Moreover, the above evidence indirectly proved that during his employment at Yixin Company, Zeng Yongfu's work positions were related to the product R&D field and that he had relevant product design and R&D capabilities and experience. Therefore, the evidence submitted by Yixin Company was insufficient to prove its claim, and it should bear the adverse consequences of failing to provide evidence. Third, the patent-in-suit was completed and filed while Zeng Yongfu was working at Yixin Company. During his employment at Yixin Company, Zeng Yongfu held positions such as Engineering Department Section Chief and Deputy Project Manager. Moreover, Wang Zhi, one of the three inventors recorded in the bibliographic data of the patent-in-suit, confirmed at the first-instance trial that Zeng Yongfu was responsible for specific implementation work during the completion of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, based on the completion time of the patent-in-suit, the inventor's work positions and duties, and the entity that filed the patent application, the patent-in-suit met the formal requirements for a service invention as provided by law. Based on the above, the first-instance court found that Zeng Yongfu was one of the inventors of the patent-in-suit.

Regarding whether the patent-in-suit had been exploited. Yixin Company claimed that the patent-in-suit had never been exploited due to technical defects. In response, the first-instance court held that: First, the technical defect claimed by Yixin Company was an unreasonable exhaust structure, causing leakage in the samples. The cause of this defect was that the exhaust pipe in the exhaust structure directly led to the outside of the bottle body, and the exhaust was uncontrolled. When the pressure inside the bottle increased or the bottle was placed horizontally and the exhaust pipe was submerged by liquid, liquid would leak out through the exhaust pipe. The technical features involved in the above defect were only additional technical features of claim 4 of the patent-in-suit. The patent-in-suit had a total of nine claims. Claim 4 referred to claim 1 or claim 3, and claims 5-9 did not refer to claim 4. In a patent claim set, each claim constitutes a complete technical solution. Even if claim 4 of the patent-in-suit had a defect, it could not prove that other claims of the same patent also had technical problems that rendered the entire patent unimplementable. Moreover, during the term of the patent-in-suit, Yixin Company filed multiple lawsuits against different defendants for infringement of the patent-in-suit. In those cases, the accused infringing products actually purchased by Yixin Company on the market were found by the court to constitute infringement because they used the patent-in-suit. That is to say, the patent-in-suit could actually be implemented and put on the market. In summary, Yixin Company's defense that the patent-in-suit could not be implemented due to technical defects was clearly inconsistent with the facts, and the first-instance court did not accept it. Second, Article 7 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law provides: "Civil entities engaged in civil activities shall adhere to the principle of good faith, act in good faith, and keep their promises." The principle of good faith, as the most important basic principle of civil law, requires civil entities to act honestly, keep their word, exercise rights and perform obligations in good faith, not to deceive or defraud, to be consistent in words and deeds, and to keep promises. Civil entities must comply with this principle in all civil activities, including civil litigation. In the aforementioned infringement lawsuits, Yixin Company claimed that the patent-in-suit had been actually put on the market and implemented, and that its products were practical and brought economic benefits to it. In most of those cases, the court ultimately ordered the defendants to compensate Yixin Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses. Therefore, Yixin Company claimed in the lawsuits against others for infringing the patent-in-suit that the patent-in-suit had been actually implemented and had generated economic benefits, but in this case, it claimed that the patent-in-suit had never been implemented. Such behavior of inconsistent statements and abuse of litigation rights clearly violated the principle of good faith, and the first-instance court did not support it. In conclusion, the patent-in-suit had been actually implemented and had generated economic benefits. The patentee Yixin Company should lawfully give reasonable remuneration to the inventor Zeng Yongfu.

(3) How to determine the amount of remuneration for the service invention in this case.

First, regarding Zeng Yongfu's application to obtain the corporate financial annual reports of Yixin Company and Dongguan Zhenlisi Company from 2007 to 2016. Apart from the report from the digital edition of Southern Metropolis Daily, Zeng Yongfu failed to submit other evidence to prove that Dongguan Zhenlisi Company had implemented the patent-in-suit. Even if the media report was true, it could not prove that the patent mentioned in the report was the patent-in-suit, and Yixin Company had denied this. Therefore, the current evidence in this case was insufficient to prove that Dongguan Zhenlisi Company had implemented the patent-in-suit, so Zeng Yongfu's application to obtain its corporate financial annual report was unfounded in law, and the first-instance court did not grant it. Since the relevant invention and utility model patent documents submitted by Yixin Company proved that it owned multiple patents related to the patent-in-suit, among which the technical solutions of the 2008 patent and the 2011 patent were improvements to the technical solution of the patent-in-suit, the patents implemented by Yixin Company should be more than just the patent-in-suit. The data in its financial annual report could not clearly distinguish the proportion of profits generated from implementing the patent-in-suit in the overall operating profit, and generally, corporate financial reports cannot distinguish specific products or patents involved. In summary, obtaining Yixin Company's financial annual report would not clarify the profits generated from implementing the patent-in-suit. This application for investigation and evidence collection was unnecessary, and the first-instance court did not grant it.

Second, Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides: "If the unit that is granted the patent right has neither agreed with the inventor or designer nor stipulated in its lawfully formulated internal rules and regulations on the method and amount of remuneration as provided in Article 16 of the Patent Law, within the term of the patent right, after the invention-creation patent is exploited, the unit shall, each year, extract no less than 2% of the operating profit from exploiting the invention or utility model patent, or no less than 0.2% of the operating profit from exploiting the design patent, as remuneration to be given to the inventor or designer, or give a lump-sum remuneration to the inventor or designer by reference to the above percentages; if the unit that is granted the patent right licenses others to exploit its patent, it shall extract no less than 10% of the royalties collected as remuneration to be given to the inventor or designer." In this case, the parties did not agree on the method and amount of remuneration for the service invention, and Yixin Company did not stipulate the method and amount of remuneration for service inventions in its internal rules and regulations. Moreover, neither party presented evidence to prove the specific operating profit generated by Yixin Company from the exploitation of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, the first-instance court comprehensively considered the following factors in determining the amount of remuneration: 1. The type of the patent-in-suit was a utility model patent; 2. There were three inventors of the patent-in-suit, and the remuneration for the service invention-creation should be divided into three shares; 3. The amount of damages for infringement determined by effective judgments in the lawsuits filed by Yixin Company related to the patent-in-suit; 4. Yixin Company filed infringement lawsuits related to the patent-in-suit almost every year from 2011 to 2016, which could to some extent prove the duration of exploitation of the patent-in-suit; 5. Yixin Company owned more than ten invention and utility model patents related to the technology of the patent-in-suit, proving that the patent-in-suit had a relatively important impact and value on Yixin Company's R&D and improvement of related technologies and products. Based on the above factors, the first-instance court determined that Yixin Company should pay Zeng Yongfu a lump-sum remuneration of RMB 200,000 for the patent-in-suit. The portion of the amount claimed by Zeng Yongfu exceeding the above amount was not supported by the first-instance court.

The first-instance court ruled: (1) Yixin Company shall pay Zeng Yongfu remuneration for the service invention creator of RMB 200,000 within ten days from the date the judgment takes legal effect; (2) Zeng Yongfu's other claims were dismissed. If the monetary obligation is not performed within the period specified in the judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 13,800 was to be borne by Zeng Yongfu in the amount of RMB 11,040 and by Yixin Company in the amount of RMB 2,760.

During the second-instance trial of this court, to prove its claims, Yixin Company submitted a summary of the cases and results of the infringement lawsuits it filed on the ground that the patent-in-suit was infringed, which it had compiled. The docket numbers of the infringement cases in this summary were not modified compared to the summary of cases and results submitted in the first instance, but the amount calculated by Yixin Company changed from RMB 1,125,000 to RMB 885,000. Zeng Yongfu's opinion on evidence was that the first-instance court correctly found that the total amount of infringement damages supported by court judgments for the patent-in-suit was RMB 1,125,000.

On June 8, 2020, Yixin Company submitted a written statement to this court, applying to withdraw its earlier appeal claim that the first-instance judgment was erroneous in calculating the amount of infringement damages, and acknowledged the first-instance judgment's finding that the total amount of infringement damages was RMB 1,125,000. The parties no longer disputed the amount of infringement damages supported by judgments in the lawsuits for infringement of the patent-in-suit filed by Yixin Company, and this court confirms this.

The facts found by the first instance court are substantially true and are confirmed by this Court.

This Court further finds: Yixin Company was established on March 31, 1993, as a limited liability company (wholly owned by a Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Macao legal person) with a registered capital of HKD 70,000,000. The company's business scope includes: production and sale of blank VHS cassette cases, 3.5-inch computer diskettes and accessories, blank computer data tape cartridges, laser heads and accessories, plastic CD outer cases (multi-pack or single-pack), plastic products, plastic molds, daily-use cosmetic packaging items, daily-use masks (non-medical), labor protection supplies, electronic products and accessories, hardware products and accessories; undertaking spray painting business. Establishment of research and development institutions to research and develop perfume bottles and daily-use cosmetic packaging items.

Opinion of the Court

The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether Zeng Yongfu has the right to claim remuneration for employee invention; (2) Whether Yixin Company should pay remuneration for employee invention to Zeng Yongfu; (3) Whether Zeng Yongfu's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations; (4) Whether the amount of remuneration for employee invention determined in the first instance judgment is appropriate.

(1) Whether Zeng Yongfu has the right to claim remuneration for employee invention

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that the first instance court erred in finding that Zeng Yongfu's start date was June 2006. Upon review, the "Resignation Employee Salary Settlement Form" and "Personnel Change Application Form" submitted by Yixin Company in the first instance both record Zeng Yongfu's start date as June 19, 2006. These forms were approved by Yixin Company's Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer, respectively. The first instance court's finding that Zeng Yongfu started working at Yixin Company in June 2006 has a factual basis and is not improper.

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that Zeng Yongfu lacked the technical capability to contribute to the patent in question, and therefore he has no right to claim remuneration for employee invention. This Court holds that Article 16 of the Patent Law provides: "The entity to which a patent is granted for a service invention-creation shall reward the inventor or designer; after the invention-creation patent is exploited, it shall give the inventor or designer a reasonable remuneration based on the scope of its popularization and application and the economic benefits obtained." Therefore, the obligor for paying remuneration for service inventions is the entity to which the patent is granted, and the payees are the inventors or designers of the service invention-creation. According to the bibliographic data recorded in the patent in question, Yixin Company is the entity to which the patent in question was granted, and Zeng Yongfu is one of the three inventors of the patent in question. Based on facts such as the completion time of the patent in question, Zeng Yongfu's start date, job position, role, and the statements of other inventors, it is sufficient to determine that Zeng Yongfu is one of the service inventors of the patent in question. Therefore, he is entitled to claim remuneration for the service invention from Yixin Company in accordance with legal provisions or agreement between the parties.

(2) Whether Yixin Company should pay remuneration for employee invention to Zeng Yongfu

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that the patent in question had a technical defect causing liquid leakage, and after several improvements, the 2008 patent and 2011 patent were applied for. The patent in question was not exploited and did not generate economic benefits, so there is no basis for Yixin Company to pay remuneration for the service invention. This Court holds that the patent in question is a portable refillable spray bottle, which has 9 claims defining technical features such as a liquid filling pipe, exhaust mechanism, sealing structure, liquid filling port, liquid filling head, spray head assembly, and a window for observing remaining liquid level. In the infringement lawsuit filed by Yixin Company against a third party for manufacturing and selling products infringing the patent in question, Yixin Company also submitted the purchased allegedly infringing products. The court also determined that the allegedly infringing technical solution fell within the scope of protection of the patent in question, and accordingly ordered the alleged infringer to bear infringement liability such as damages. Therefore, this Court finds it difficult to accept Yixin Company's argument that the patent in question has technical structural defects and cannot be exploited.

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that the first instance court erred in finding that the patent in question had been exploited. This Court holds that, according to Article 11 of the Patent Law, a patentee not only has the right to exploit the patent itself but also has the right to prohibit others from exploiting the patent without permission. Moreover, prohibiting others from exploiting the patent without permission does not require the patentee to have actually exploited the patent as a necessary condition for rights enforcement. Based on the facts found, when Yixin Company enforced its rights against the infringement of the patent in question, it explicitly stated to the court that "since the patented product was put on the market, it gained consumer favor due to its strong practicality, bringing economic benefits to Yixin Company, and the alleged infringer exploited the patent in question without Yixin Company's permission." This statement made by Yixin Company in the infringement lawsuit, that the patent in question had been exploited and the patented product had generated economic benefits, is a statement of objective facts. According to the principle of good faith, it should be presumed that Yixin Company had exploited the technical solution of the patent in question. The first instance court determined that Yixin Company had exploited the patent in question and obtained income based on Yixin Company's violation of the principle of good faith, which was not improper. This Court affirms this finding.

Yixin Company's appeal that the first instance court determined the existence of exploitation of the patent in question solely because Yixin Company filed an infringement lawsuit based on the patent does not correspond to the facts found in the first instance judgment.

Regarding Yixin Company's appeal that, according to the Patent Law and its Implementing Regulations, the "exploitation" after which the entity to which the patent is granted gives remuneration for a service invention refers to the actual act of putting a patented product on the market, and that the compensation obtained from the infringement lawsuit for the patent in question should not be considered as income obtained from exploiting the patent. This Court holds that Article 16 of the Patent Law and Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provide that after an invention-creation patent is exploited, the entity to which the patent is granted shall give the inventor or designer a reasonable remuneration based on the scope of its popularization and application and the economic benefits obtained. If the entity to which the patent is granted has not agreed with the inventor or designer, nor stipulated in its legally established rules and regulations the method and amount of remuneration, then within the validity period of the patent right, after exploiting the invention-creation patent, each year it shall extract no less than 2% of the operating profit from the exploitation of the invention or utility model patent as remuneration to the inventor... According to the above legal provisions, the entity to which the patent is granted shall pay remuneration to the service inventor or designer because the entity exploits the patent and obtains economic benefits from the exploitation. The emphasis is on the situation where the patent is exploited to generate economic benefits, and the entity that obtains such economic benefits shall give reasonable remuneration to the inventor or designer. In this case, Yixin Company, as the entity to which the patent was granted, obtained damages from enforcing its rights based on the patent in question. This is income obtained by the patentee by prohibiting others from exploiting the patent without permission. After deducting necessary costs of enforcement and expenses, this economic benefit should be considered as the operating profit referred to in Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law. It is legally justified to base reasonable remuneration for the inventor on this amount. Therefore, the RMB 1,125,000 in damages obtained by Yixin Company from the infringement lawsuit for infringement of the patent in question, after deducting necessary enforcement costs and expenses, should serve as one of the bases for paying Zeng Yongfu's remuneration for the service invention. Yixin Company's argument that the amount of damages from the infringement lawsuit it filed should not be used as a basis for measuring remuneration for the service invention is not supported by this Court.

(3) Whether Zeng Yongfu's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that Zeng Yongfu's claim for remuneration for the service invention exceeded the statute of limitations, and that the first instance court erred in its determination. This Court holds that the right to claim remuneration for a service invention is a creditor's claim. Its statute of limitations begins when the entity to which the patent is granted should pay the remuneration and the inventor or designer knows or should know that they are entitled to the remuneration. In this case, the starting point for Zeng Yongfu's claim for remuneration should be when he knew or should have known that Yixin Company had exploited the patent in question and obtained economic benefits. Upon review, Zeng Yongfu filed this lawsuit on October 11, 2017, requesting a one-time payment of remuneration for the service invention. Although Zeng Yongfu submitted to the first instance court a report about Yixin Company's exploitation of the patent in question published in the Southern Metropolis Daily on October 21, 2013, there is no evidence that Zeng Yongfu learned of the content of the report on the date of publication and thereby learned that Yixin Company had obtained licensing fees or operating profits. Therefore, the date of publication of the report cannot be used as the starting point for Zeng Yongfu's claim for remuneration in this case. Yixin Company also has no evidence that Zeng Yongfu knew of the exploitation and profitability of the patent in question in 2013, so its appeal that Zeng Yongfu's request for remuneration should be limited to the period from January 1, 2015, to May 23, 2017, is not supported by this Court.

As stated above, another basis for determining that Yixin Company should pay Zeng Yongfu remuneration for the service invention in this case is that the damages obtained by Yixin Company from the patent infringement lawsuit for the patent in question should be included in the calculation base for the service invention remuneration. According to the evidence on record, the infringement lawsuits filed by Yixin Company for infringement of the patent in question were separate lawsuits, not continuous acts. Therefore, the statute of limitations for Zeng Yongfu's claim for payment of service invention remuneration should start from the date he first made the request and Yixin Company refused to perform. His filing of this lawsuit with the first instance court for a one-time payment of service invention remuneration has not exceeded the statute of limitations and is protected by law. Yixin Company's appeal ground regarding exceeding the statute of limitations is not supported by this Court.

(4) Whether the amount of remuneration for employee invention determined in the first instance judgment is appropriate

This Court holds that Yixin Company and Zeng Yongfu did not agree on the method and amount of remuneration for the service invention of the patent in question, nor did Yixin Company stipulate the method and amount of payment in its rules and regulations. Regarding the method of paying remuneration for service inventions, the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provide two methods: annual payment or one-time payment. Regarding the one-time payment, the performance period is stipulated as "within the validity period of the patent right, after the patent is exploited." In this case, Zeng Yongfu's request for a one-time payment of remuneration is legally justified.

Yixin Company appealed, arguing that the amount of remuneration determined by the first instance court was erroneous, claiming that it did not take into account Yixin Company's costs of rights enforcement and that Yixin Company did not profit from enforcement. This Court holds that the first instance court did not use the amount of damages awarded to Yixin Company in the judgment as the operating profit from Yixin Company's exploitation of the patent in question to calculate the service invention remuneration. Therefore, there is no issue of failing to deduct enforcement costs or related expenses when calculating the remuneration. As stated above, Yixin Company has exploited the patent in question and obtained economic benefits. It also admitted to having continuously improved the patented technology and actually produced improved patented products. Regarding the exploitation and operating profit of the patent in question, Yixin Company, as the entity to which the patent was granted, should have controlled this information, but in this case it denied exploiting the patent in question and did not submit relevant evidence. Since the operating profit obtained from exploiting the patent in question is difficult to ascertain, and as stated above, the damages obtained by Yixin Company through patent enforcement also constitute its economic benefits and should be considered the operating profit referred to in Article 78 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, thereby serving as one of the factors for determining the amount of service invention remuneration. Therefore, comprehensively considering multiple factors such as: the type of patent in question is a utility model patent; the patent involves three inventors; the validity period of the patent was from May 23, 2007, to May 23, 2017; the impact and value of the patent on the research, development, and improvement of Yixin Company's related technical products; the inevitable expenses incurred by Yixin Company in the enforcement lawsuit; the actual amount of damages awarded to Yixin Company in the judgment that were actually received through enforcement, etc., the first instance court's determination that Yixin Company should pay Zeng Yongfu RMB 200,000 as remuneration for the service invention is substantially appropriate. Yixin Company's appeal argument that the amount determined by the first instance court was erroneous is not supported by this Court.

In conclusion, Yixin Company's appeal grounds are untenable and should be dismissed. The first instance judgment has substantially clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Item (1) of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 4,300 shall be borne by the appellant, Dongguan Yixin Magnetic Disc Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
